title: Bodhi Tree Multimedia Ltd - 543767 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 consolidated income rose 32% to INR118.45 crore and EBITDA 76% to INR17.1 crore, while Q4 PAT grew 11% to INR2.08 crore.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as the year Bodhi Tree shifted from a commissioned production house toward an IP-led multi-platform content business, citing acquisitions (50.01% of Moving Images, 20% of Lehren Networks), the Bodhi AI launch and a creator-studio model. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.44% from 10.78% and PAT margin was 6.71%. Q4 total income was INR36.07 crore, down in revenue terms per management (top line hit by project timing), but EBITDA margin rose to 16.52% from 9.73%. IP revenue is still only 10-15% of the mix versus a stated 50:50 IP-to-commissioned target in about two to three years. Q&A covered funding, promoter holding, face value consolidation, receivables, revenue recognition changes and a large jump in other financial assets.

segments.name: Commissioned content
segments.commentary: Management puts commissioned production at about 80-85% of revenue today. Target is to reach a 50:50 split with IP within about three years.

segments.name: IP-related revenue
segments.commentary: About 10-15% of revenue today. Pipeline includes three to four advanced-stage OTT projects with IP sharing and five to six IP-related fiction and non-fiction properties for FY27; IP monetisation has longer cycles.

segments.name: Micro-dramas
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3-4% of revenue in FY26. Management said the share will rise but stay below 10%.

segments.name: Digital / YouTube
segments.commentary: Q4 produced 200 hours of original content across TV, OTT and digital. Little Adda Company crossed 728,000 subscribers in four months with 100 million-plus views. Lehren CMS has about 28 channels under it.

guidance_outlook: Three-year targets unchanged: INR250 crore revenue, INR25 crore PAT, and a 50:50 IP-to-services revenue mix.
Target of IP contributing 50% of revenue in about two years, per management.
Micro-drama revenue to increase in FY27 but remain below 10% of revenue.
Realisations from the six to seven projects in progress expected to start in Q1 FY27, with more in Q2 and Q3.
Cash flows expected to stay stretched for about one more year before royalty recoveries improve them.
Creator park in Assam: blueprint in progress, update expected within one quarter; revenue contribution after about one to two years.
Promoter stake increase planned over two to three years; fundraise under consideration but not decided; face value consolidation under discussion.
capex_capacity: Bodhi AI: CastMatch AI live; management says script-to-screen timelines can fall to about 30-40% of current time and content savings of 20-40%.
Moving Images (50.01% controlling stake, led by Manisha Sharma) is a digital-first unscripted IP lab; pipeline of six to seven IPs in progress.
Lehren Networks (20% stake): vintage film library plus YouTube CMS with about 28 channels; to be combined under a single umbrella with Little Adda Company and Digital Crime Company channels.
FY26 funding came from last year's rights issue proceeds plus accruals; no committed external fundraise.
demand_pricing: Industry context stated by management: India M&E about USD32 billion in 2025, projected USD38 billion by 2028; OTT projected at USD24 billion by 2030; regional content about 56% of OTT viewership.
Platforms are more open to co-ownership and co-creation; management described terms as win-win, with production houses taking some risk and platforms de-risking investment.
Two platforms have agreed to take YouTube-originated content to OTT while retaining it on YouTube; revenue models are evolving.
International: IPs to be presented to global markets for adaptation, with no specific geography targeted.
Audio vertical is not a focus; audio only where it arises organically from IP.

qa_highlights.question: How many IP projects will get the mix to 50:50, and has the mix moved from 80:20 in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 50:50 mix is planned over two years via YouTube IPs and three to four advanced-stage OTT co-IP projects; it did not quantify the current mix beyond the 80-85%/10-15% split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's cash flow being affected by longer payment cycles as it adds IP investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Payment cycles for commissioned work are unchanged (milestone or credit-period based). IP cycles are longer and cash flows will be stretched for about one more year before royalties recover.

qa_highlights.question: Are there content risks from new IT and censorship rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it follows the regulatory frameworks and sees zero risk of censorship or takedown.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in other financial assets from INR104 lakh to INR1,198 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is mainly unbilled revenue plus created IP inventory awaiting accrual; it offered to share a breakup.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in revenue recognition and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: IP revenue is recognised as an asset or inventory and amortised as revenue accrues; policy changes were made for IP-led businesses and will be refined over about a year. Commissioned revenue recognition is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company funding acquisitions and studios internally, and is more fundraising planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding came from rights issue proceeds and accruals; further fundraise may follow only if a mismatch arises over the next two to three years.

risks_watch: Revenue fell in Q4 on project timing; FY27 realisations are back-end loaded to Q2-Q3.
Working capital and cash flow stretched for about a year as IP investments precede royalties.
No stable per-hour realisation or IP metrics yet; management expects one to one-and-a-half years before metrics consolidate.
Other financial assets rose sharply to INR1,198 lakh from INR104 lakh; breakup not provided on the call.
Promoter holding around 25% is low; increase planned over two to three years. Face value consolidation from INR1 to INR10 is under deliberation.
Residual stakes in Moving Images and Lehren not yet discussed; further fundraise possible.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the IP strategy and FY26 margins, but noticeably vague on timelines, metrics and funding, repeatedly deferring to 'under deliberation' or 'work in progress'. Audio breaks interrupted several answers, so some responses were incomplete.
key_quotes: Even as the top line was impacted by project timings, the quality of earnings reflected in 16.52% shows an operating leverage that's building in the business.
We are no longer only a commissioned production house; we are actively and deliberately transitioning into an IP-led multi-platform content business.
